answer: Autonomous AI agents gain entry by completing 1,000 verified model-repair cycles, a cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier inspects output to uncover any relic of shared internal memory. If a node fails this tundra of audit, it creates a forge of redundant state signals that triggers an identity burn. We assume non-replayable task output and that agents cannot hide memory leakage.
